lines.speaker: d
lines.text: One hole on a Canadian island has swallowed two centuries of treasure hunts.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Diggers said they hit a log platform every ten feet.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Some were topped with charcoal, putty, even coconut fiber.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: At ninety feet, a flat stone carved with strange symbols.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then something hard at ninety-eight feet. By morning, the pit held sixty feet of water.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: A young Franklin Roosevelt dug here too.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In nineteen seventy-one, a camera went down a shaft about two hundred thirty-five feet deep. None of what crews claimed to see was ever confirmed.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: But geologists say the Money Pit may be a natural sinkhole, and the logs, fallen trees.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: And the carved stone? The only drawing of its symbols dates from nineteen forty-nine.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Still, no treasure has ever come out of it.
